corrections.issue: The 'because few participants absorb flow' reason is not stated; the host only says a dollar into equities multiplies rather than notches the price (and that this is the Bouchaud/Wigglesworth FT lunch article).
corrections.fix: Under the inelastic market hypothesis (Bouchaud, CFM, as described by the host from an FT article), a dollar flowing into equities multiplies the price effect rather than moving it by one dollar's worth, so flows can dominate returns.

corrections.issue: Beer calls the 300 bps an 'efficiency advantage' and 'outperformance' of the replication product versus single managers over 10 years, not a cost advantage.
corrections.fix: Pairing against replication is costly because DBMF has outperformed single managers by about 300 bps a year over 10 years (more for investable mutual fund or UCITS peers), so the short leg bleeds and timing the swings is unpredictable.

corrections.issue: Beer says '80 to 90% of ETFs' beat the average mutual fund/hedge fund in 2024-25 (his HedgeNordic article); the scope is ETFs versus fund peers, not specifically simple replication products versus managed futures peers.
corrections.fix: In 2024 and 2025 about 80-90% of ETFs beat the average mutual fund or hedge fund peer by a lot, which Beer calls statistically awkward and takes as a hint of a structural cause (cost, liquidity, simplicity).

corrections.issue: Garbled: the -6% March 2020 loss is the multistrat fund NAV; Beer says with about 5x leverage that equals only about -1% across the underlying unlevered portfolio.
corrections.fix: Multistrategy hedge funds had a worst month of about -6% (March 2020, per Beer), equal to roughly -1% on the underlying unlevered book at 5x leverage, so the engine was very resilient to the COVID crash.

corrections.issue: The ending is ambiguous: Beer says the multistrat model cannot be run outside a hedge fund structure or when clients can redeem every quarter, not that it cannot be 'replicated with quarterly liquidity'.
corrections.fix: Liquid-alt multi-strategy mutual funds returned under 3% a year over 10 years after about 200 bps fees (an embarrassing failure), and Beer says multistrat returns need the hedge-fund structure and capital that clients cannot pull every quarter.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader caught the main themes and most numbers across all 19 chunks; missed attributed views (Mike Green, Pivotal Path data quality), the CalPERS bucket closure, CTA index dispersion, the 2022 incentive-fee point and several caveats (dead-money risk, lookback hypothesis).
